newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian call money ends lower, gilts unchanged.
newsitem.headline: Indian call money ends lower, gilts unchanged.

text.p: Indian call money rates closed lower at 3.50-4.00 percent on Monday after opening the day at 4.50 percent, dealers said.
"Call rates opened higher on Monday and settled down to 4.00 percent," said a dealer at a financial institution.
"We expect call rates to rise as the advance tax payment of 40 billion rupees is expected to go out of the system towards the end of the current fortnight (December 20)," he said.
"Banks will borrow 90 to 95 percent of the total reserve, as they feel the market would tighten towards the end of next week," he said.

"If the advance tax outflow is 60 billion rupees the call rates will move to 8.0 percent, if it is 40 billion rupees it will rally to 5.0-6.0 percent and below that will see steady levels at 4.0 percent," he added.
Yields on government securities remained unchanged for short to medium term paper, dealers said.
The reduction in the latest auctioned 91-day treasury bill cut-off by 10 basis points improved the sentiment in the securities market, a dealer said.
He said volume on National Stock Exchange rose to 1.73 billion rupees on Monday from Saturday's 1.11 billion rupees.
Yield on 13.50 percent 1997 stock and 12.50 percent 2004 was unchanged at 10.68 percent and 13.75 percent respectively, dealers said.
Yield on treasury bills maturing in March 1997 fell by 5.0 basis points on Monday to 7.85 percent for March 8, while it was unchanged at 7.70 percent for March 1, dealers said.
Yield on treasury bills maturing in Decemeber rose by 2.0 basis points to 10.25 percent, they said.
"Secondary market yields on institutional bonds have eased up by one to two percentage points after the October monetary policy announcement," said a dealer at lending institution.
He said the secondary market activity for institutional bonds have also picked gradually.
There was no activity in certificate of deposits and commercial paper on Monday, a dealer said.
